title: A transient Resend failure permanently fails a queued email: all attempts burn in one drain pass, no backoff, no transient/permanent split
claim_actual: A row whose send fails transiently is requeued with status 'queued' and its original createdAt, so the very next iteration of the SAME drain pass re-selects it (it is still the oldest eligible row under orderBy [priority asc, createdAt asc]). Four failures in four consecutive iterations, seconds apart, hit MAX_ATTEMPTS and the row is terminally 'failed'. One BATCH=8 pass during an outage terminally kills 2 rows; every authenticated page view spawns another pass (layout after()), so a ~5-minute Resend outage or 429 storm at launch traffic converts the entire backlog, resets included, to permanent 'failed'. Nothing retries after the outage ends ('failed' is terminal); recovery is the admin clicking retryMail one row at a time. A reset requester was already told { ok: true } ('check your inbox') and sees nothing, ever.
evidence: The loop re-picks the same row: `const next = await prisma.outboundEmail.findFirst({ where: { status: "queued", kind: { in: eligibleKinds }, attempts: { lt: MAX_ATTEMPTS } }, orderBy: [{ priority: "asc" }, { createdAt: "asc" }], ... })` (461-475) — a requeued row keeps createdAt so it stays at the head. claimAndSend increments attempts on every claim (`attempts: { increment: 1 }`, 162) and computes `const afterFailure = spent >= MAX_ATTEMPTS ? "failed" : "queued"` (174); every failure path writes `status: afterFailure` (224, 231) with no delay, no nextAttemptAt, and no inspection of the error class — sendMail collapses a Resend 429, a 5xx and a genuinely invalid address into the same `{ ok: false, error }` (email.ts:188-199). There is no code path that returns a 'failed' row to 'queued' when the day or the provider recovers.
orchestrator_note: drainMailQueue loop re-picks the same requeued row immediately, burning MAX_ATTEMPTS back-to-back; claimAndSend has no transient vs permanent distinction. A 30s Resend brownout permanently fails every in-flight verify/reset.

title: Deleting a member cascades away every Catch-up question they asked, removing every OTHER member's answers to it from published Rounds
claim_actual: CatchupPrompt.authorId is onDelete: Cascade, and CatchupEntry.promptId is onDelete: Cascade. Purging member A deletes every prompt A authored in ANY catch-up (not just ones A created), which cascades every entry anyone wrote answering those prompts. In a 30-person Round where A asked one of the questions, 30 people's answers (text, photos, hearts) silently disappear from the published Round. The cascaded entries' images are also not collected by collectImageUrls (it only reads entries where authorId = the purged user), so those photos are stranded in R2.

title: Account purge deletes DB rows first then R2 bytes best-effort from an in-memory URL list; any crash/timeout mid-loop permanently orphans images
claim_actual: purgeUserAccount collects URLs in a local array, deletes the rows in a transaction, then loops `for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; }` (account-purge.ts:109-112). Three defects compound: (1) delImageByKey swallows every error (`catch { /* best-effort cleanup */ }`, storage.ts:225-227), so a transient R2 429/500 during the loop silently skips the object — and because the pointing rows are already gone, the file's own comment admits 'afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects' (account-purge.ts:79-81): the miss is permanent and the bytes stay publicly fetchable at pub-*.r2.dev, which is exactly the pre-H9 failure this module exists to close. (2) `deleted` counts loop iterations, not successes, and flows into the audit detail `${purged.imagesDeleted} stored image(s) removed` (retention.ts:132, admin-actions.ts:70), so the compliance record can state images were removed when none were. (3) If the serverless function crashes or hits its duration ceiling between the row transaction and the end of the loop (see the unbounded-sweep finding), every remaining URL is lost with the process. There is no persisted work list, no retry, and no orphan-reconciliation sweep on the R2 side.
evidence: account-purge.ts:108-113: `let deleted = 0; for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; } return { ok: true, imagesDeleted: deleted };` — increment is unconditional. storage.ts:218-228: `export async function delImageByKey(key: string): Promise<void> { try { ... DeleteObjectCommand ... } catch { // best-effort cleanup } }` — void return, error swallowed, caller cannot know. account-purge.ts:77-81 comment: 'URLs are collected FIRST, because the cascade takes the pointing rows with it and afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects' — i.e. the in-memory array is the last copy. retention.ts:131-132 writes `"${purged.imagesDeleted} stored image(s) removed"` into the account.purge audit row.
orchestrator_note: purgeUserAccount: prisma.$transaction deletes rows, then for-loop delImage over urls collected before the delete. No resume, no persisted worklist. Unbounded sequential R2 deletes vs Vercel duration ceiling.

title: R2 delete failures are swallowed with no log (delImageByKey empty catch) and purge counts delete ATTEMPTS as deletions — the audit line lies
claim_actual: delImageByKey's catch block is completely empty — not even the repo's own 'loud in dev' rule is honoured, making it the one catch site in the codebase that violates the stated contract. purgeUserAccount then counts `deleted += 1` for every URL regardless of outcome, and both the retention sweep and adminDeleteUser write that count into the audit log as fact. If R2 has a bad minute (or credentials rotate, or the bucket name env var drifts) during a purge, zero objects are deleted, the rows that pointed at them are already gone, the images stay live at their public pub-*.r2.dev URLs forever, and every record says the purge removed them.
evidence: storage.ts:218-228: `export async function delImageByKey(key: string): Promise<void> { try { ... } catch { // best-effort cleanup } }` — empty catch, no console.error even in development. account-purge.ts:108-113: `let deleted = 0; for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; } return { ok: true, imagesDeleted: deleted };` — the counter increments unconditionally because delImage never throws. The header comment on purgeUserAccount even says 'the audit entry the CALLER writes records how many objects were actually removed' (account-purge.ts:85-86) — which this makes untrue. Consumed as fact at retention.ts:127-133 (`detail: "...${purged.imagesDeleted} stored image(s) removed"`) and admin-actions.ts:64-73. The irreversibility is documented in the same file: 'URLs are collected FIRST, because the cascade takes the pointing rows with it and afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects' (account-purge.ts:80-82). Every other delete caller (deletePost, declinePhoto, adminRemovePhoto, updateAvatar) shares the same invisible-failure property, but the purge is where it becomes unrecoverable.
orchestrator_note: storage.ts delImageByKey catch{} empty; purgeUserAccount increments deleted per attempt regardless of success.

claim_actual: They land on /feed, always. The parameter the proxy writes is never read by anything.

The login success path (login-client.tsx:403) is `window.location.href = nextPathFromLocation();`, and nextPathFromLocation reads only `next`: `safeNextPath(new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("next"), fallback)` (next-path.ts:35). title: An admin can block or delete their own or the last admin's account with no guard — permanent lockout of the whole admin surface
claim_actual: adminBlockUser and adminDeleteUser have no self-check and no last-admin check. The owner's own row is reachable at /admin/people/<own-id> and PersonDetail renders Block, Delete and Merge for it unconditionally (no current-admin id is even passed to the component). Blocking yourself takes effect on the very next request: the session callback in src/lib/auth.ts:277 invalidates any session whose row reads isBlocked, and authorize() (auth.ts:155) refuses a blocked account at login, so the sole admin can never unblock himself. The block dialog's copy makes it worse: "You can undo this from the same button" (person-detail.tsx:373) is false for self-block.
evidence: adminBlockUser body is only: `const actor = await requireAdminActor(); ... await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: userId }, data: { isBlocked: block, credentialVersion: { increment: 1 } } });` — no comparison of userId against actor.actorId and no count of remaining admins. adminDeleteUser likewise goes straight to `purgeUserAccount(userId)`. Contrast adminSetRole (people/actions.ts:216-225) which counts admins and refuses the last demotion, and whose comment explains the stake: "demoting the only admin locks everybody out of moderation permanently, and the only way back would be editing the database by hand" — the identical lockout exists via block and delete and is unguarded. Recovery script scripts/dev/set-password.mjs --admin restores role but nothing documents clearing isBlocked, and delete is unrecoverable.
orchestrator_note: admin-actions block/delete lack a last-admin / self guard (adminSetRole has a check-then-act one, block/delete none).

title: All 12 /admin pages rely on the layout gate, which does not re-run on page-segment RSC requests: a demoted admin keeps reading admin data mid-session
claim_actual: requireAdminPage() runs only in admin/layout.tsx. Grep confirms none of the 12 admin page.tsx files (nor their query helpers, e.g. lib/admin-people-query.ts) call auth()/requireAdminPage — they are bare prisma reads. In App Router partial rendering, a navigation request renders only the segments the client's Next-Router-State-Tree marks as changed: node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/walk-tree-with-flight-router-state.js gates rendering on `renderComponentsOnThisLevel` derived from the client-sent flightRouterState, and the staleTimes doc states 'shared layouts won't automatically be refetched on every navigation, only the page segment that changes'. Two consequences: (1) an admin demoted mid-session who is already inside /admin keeps soft-navigating between admin subpages and receiving fresh admin data — the layout gate never re-runs and the pages never check (role demotion does not bump credentialVersion, and even if it did, no code on these renders reads the session at all); (2) a regular member who crafts an RSC request whose router-state-tree marks the admin layout segment as already-known may receive the page segment's flight data — the proxy only checks that a session cookie EXISTS, and nothing else in the render path checks anything.
evidence: src/app/(main)/admin/layout.tsx: `await requireAdminPage(); const counts = await loadAdminCounts();` is the only gate. src/app/(main)/admin/people/page.tsx: `const [page, total] = await Promise.all([loadPeoplePage(filters), prisma.user.count({ where: peopleWhere(filters) })]);` — no session read. lib/admin.ts's own comment concedes the design: 'A layout guard is navigation, not authorisation' — but applies that reasoning only to server actions, while the PAGES render the same protected data. walk-tree-with-flight-router-state.js:58-119: `const renderComponentsOnThisLevel = ...` / `if (renderComponentsOnThisLevel) {` — the server renders only what the client's header claims is missing.
orchestrator_note: SUSPECTED: admin/layout.tsx is the only role gate; RSC segment requests may skip layout re-eval. Needs live proof.

title: Onboarding + settings avatar and Catch-up answer photos ship raw bytes (up to 15MB / 5MBx3) through Server Actions past Vercel's ~4.5MB body cap
claim_actual: PhotoStep validates only `if (file.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024)` and then ships the original bytes straight into the updateAvatar server action: `const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); const result = await updateAvatar(fd);`. There is no crop dialog and no downscaleImage call on this path (AttachImageDialog explicitly has 'no opinion about size/format limits'). On Vercel, request bodies above ~4.5MB are rejected by the PLATFORM (413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) before the function runs — the `serverActions: { bodySizeLimit: "25mb" }` in next.config.ts only lifts Next's own guard and cannot raise Vercel's cap. So any photo between ~4.5MB and 15MB passes every client check, then dies at the edge; the action never executes, the client's `result.error` handling never gets a structured error, and the member sees a generic failure on the very first flow they touch. The project has already diagnosed this exact hazard twice elsewhere: image-downscale.ts's header comment ('a route handler's request body is hard-capped at about 4.5MB... a normal phone photo (often 5 to 12MB) sailed past the client check and then died at Vercel's edge with an opaque failure') and letterhead-profile.tsx ('a 6MB phone photo could die on Vercel's ~4.5MB serverless body cap'), whose avatar path was fixed with a client-side crop that produces a small webp blob. The onboarding step reuses the same server a
evidence: src/components/onboarding/steps/photo-step.tsx:42-49 `if (file.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024) { toast.error("Photo must be under 15MB"); return; } setBusy(true); const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); const result = await updateAvatar(fd);` — raw file, no downscale, no crop. src/components/settings/actions.ts:20 `const MAX_AVATAR_INPUT = 15 * 1024 * 1024; // 15MB input` — the server-side cap promises 15MB but can never see more than ~4.5MB on Vercel. next.config.ts:111-112 `serverActions: { bodySizeLimit: "25mb" }` — configures Next, not the platform. src/components/profile/letterhead-profile.tsx:363-365 comment: 'the old path shipped the ORIGINAL bytes... a 6MB phone photo could die on Vercel's ~4.5MB serverless body cap' — the same team's own statement of the failure mode this step still has.

title: All five like/vote/bookmark toggle actions are check-then-write with no P2002/P2025 handling: a double-tap throws a raw error and desyncs the UI
claim_actual: toggleLike, toggleBookmark, toggleCommentLike, votePoll (feed/actions.ts) and togglePhotoLove (collection/actions.ts) each do findUnique → create/delete/update with NO try/catch. Two rapid invocations (mobile double-tap, two tabs — post-card.tsx handleLike at 134-145 has zero in-flight guard: no busy state, no disable) both read `existing = null` and both create; the loser throws PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2002 out of the action. Symmetrically, both reading `existing` and both deleting throws P2025. The client code only handles `result.error` (post-card.tsx:140 `if (result.error)`), so the throw becomes an unhandled promise rejection: no toast, no revert, and the two optimistic flips leave the heart showing the opposite of the database (handleLike toggled state twice while the DB holds one like). Additionally togglePhotoLove does not verify the photo exists, so a stale photoId (photo declined meanwhile) throws P2003 the same unhandled way. The catchups counterpart toggleEntryLove has the identical race but is wrapped in runAction (catchups/actions.ts:162-172), degrading to a friendly `{ error }` — the feed/collection five lack even that. Complete class-1 uniqueness map produced by this sweep: BACKED+HANDLED: User.email (registerUser P2002 catch), Catchup.groupId (createCatchup P2002 catch), Report[reporterId,reportedUserId] (reportUser P2002 catch), GroupMember[groupId,user
evidence: feed/actions.ts:477-494: `const existing = await prisma.like.findUnique({ where: { userId_postId: ... } }); if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.like.create({ data: { userId: session.user.id, postId } });` — no try/catch anywhere in the function; schema.prisma:465 `@@unique([userId, postId])` guarantees the loser throws. post-card.tsx:134-145: `async function handleLike() { const next = !liked; setLiked(next); setLikeCount(...); const result = await toggleLike(post.id); if (result.error) {...} }` — a thrown action means `result` never exists and the rejection escapes the handler.
orchestrator_note: toggleLike/toggleCommentLike/toggleBookmark/togglePhotoLove/votePoll: find-then-create, unhandled unique/notfound; no client rejection handler.

title: Deleting or editing a post from the feed never updates the on-screen list: the stale/old card stays until a full reload
claim_actual: Nothing visible happens. Every surface that renders PostCard (main feed, group feed, profile Posts/Letters tabs, Saved) holds its posts in client useState populated by the loadPosts/loadSavedPosts server actions. revalidatePath('/feed') in deletePost/editPost only re-renders the server component tree; the client `posts` state persists, so the deleted post remains on screen (clicking delete again errors) and the edited card keeps the pre-edit content until the member navigates away and back.
evidence: post-card.tsx handleDelete does nothing locally on success: `const result = await deletePost(post.id); if (result.error) toast.error(result.error);` — no setRemoved, no callback, no router.refresh. Contrast the ADMIN path four lines below, which the author knew needed it: `async function handleModerationConfirm(note) { const result = await adminRemovePost(...); if (!result.error) setRemoved(true); }` with the comment 'Removed optimistically ... rather than waiting on the revalidatePath round trip.' EditPostDialog on success only does `toast.success(...); onClose();` — PostCard renders `post.content` from props, which never change. The lists are client state: post-feed.tsx `const [posts, setPosts] = useState<PostData[]>([]);` filled by `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => { setPosts(data.posts); ... })`; only creation refreshes it (feed-column.tsx `onPosted={() => setReloadKey((k) => k + 1)}` — there is no onDeleted/onEdited equivalent, confirmed by grep: reloadKey's only bump site is onPosted). deletePost's revalidatePath (actions.ts:340) cannot reach this state.
orchestrator_note: post-feed client posts state has no removal/update path after delete/edit server action.

title: No client component handles a rejected server action anywhere: one network blip / deploy skew / auth redirect strands the UI (infinite skeletons, stuck buttons)
claim_actual: Almost every other await-an-action site assumes resolution. Consequences by class: (a) ETERNAL LOADING — post-feed.tsx initial load `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => {...})` has no .catch, so a rejection leaves `loading` true forever: the app's main page shows skeletons with no retry path. Same shape in comments-section initial load, saved-posts-feed, profile-author-feed, collection-client. (b) WEDGED CONTROLS — comments-section handleSubmit: `setSubmitting(true); ... await createComment(formData); ... setSubmitting(false)` with no try: a throw leaves submitting true and the comment box disabled forever; identical pattern wedges poll-display (whole poll disabled), message-composer Send, create-post-form Post/Save-as-draft (stranding the typed letter), notification-bell load-more (loadingMoreRef stuck true kills infinite scroll), comments-section IO callback (same ref), directory/collection/people-list Load more, people-panel keeper/remove/add, extend-deadline-card, console-collecting submit, accept-invite, publish-now-button, keeper-settings, letterhead-profile uploadAvatarBlob/handlePhotoRemove (photoBusy stuck). title: Letter autosave fails silently: on any error the desk keeps saying 'Saving...', and a fresh never-saved letter is lost entirely on nav/close/crash
claim_actual: Two gaps. (1) Resumed-draft autosave: `const result = await editPost(postId, fd); if (!result.error) onAutosaveState?.("saved")` — when result.error is set (e.g. 'Not authenticated' after the session was revoked, which the app's own credentialVersion mechanism does instantly on a password reset or deletion request from another device) NOTHING happens: no toast, no state change, the desk chrome stays on 'Saving...' (letter-desk.tsx:55) while every subsequent autosave also fails; a transport rejection additionally goes unhandled (no try/catch). The writer continues for an hour believing the letter is persisting; navigating away loses everything since the last good save. (2) A FRESH letter at /letters/new has no row, so no autosave, no localStorage fallback, and no beforeunload guard (grep for beforeunload across components/posts and components/letters returns nothing) — a crash, an accidental Back, or a session end discards the entire composition.
evidence: create-post-form.tsx:218-227: `autosaveTimer.current = setTimeout(async () => { ... onAutosaveState?.("saving"); ... const result = await editPost(postId, fd); if (!result.error) onAutosaveState?.("saved"); }, 2500);` — the error branch is empty and the await is uncaught. letter-desk.tsx:54-56 renders `{saveState === "saving" ? "Saving..." : ...}` from exactly that callback. The session-revocation interaction is real and by design: auth.ts session callback returns invalid (→ auth() null → editPost returns { error: "Not authenticated" }) the moment credentialVersion changes (auth.ts:277-281), e.g. resetPassword's `credentialVersion: { increment: 1 }` (email-actions.ts:280).
orchestrator_note: autosave error path leaves 'Saving...' with no surface; no draft persistence for an unsaved letter/long post.

title: Composer Post/Save stays enabled while photo uploads are in flight: the post publishes without its photos
claim_actual: On a slow connection a member attaches photos (spinner on the photo icon), types, and hits Post before the batch finishes: the post is created from the current `images` state — without the in-flight photos. When handleImageFiles later completes, it appends the uploaded URLs to the now-cleared arrays, so thumbnails reappear inside the empty, collapsed composer; the next post the member writes silently carries the previous post's photos. title: 'This week in Letters' rail surfaces city-scoped letters to every member sitewide — content leak + guaranteed 404 on click-through
claim_actual: The feed rail's LettersModule picks the newest main-feed letter with NO viewer context and NO cityScope filter, so a city-scoped letter's title, excerpt, author and read time are shown to every member on /feed. An out-of-city member who clicks it hits the reading page's canViewCityScope check and gets notFound() — a teaser to a 404, for as long as that letter is the newest of the week.
evidence: letters-module.tsx where clause is only: `where: { kind: "letter", isHidden: false, groupId: null, ...PUBLISHED_ONLY, createdAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - WEEK_MS) } }` — it selects `title, content, author` and renders `letterTitle(letter.title, letter.content)` plus `plainExcerpt(letter.content)`. title: Like/comment/reply notifications link to /feed#<postId> (never scrolls, wrong for group posts/letters); admin bell links to retired /admin?thread=
claim_actual: All four write sites hard-code `link: \`/feed#${postId}\`` regardless of the post's kind or groupId. (1) Group posts never appear in the main feed (loadPosts filters `groupId: null`), so the link lands on /feed with nothing to show. (2) A letter's comments are not rendered in the feed (the feed shows a compact letter card; the thread lives at /letters/[id]), so a comment notification on a letter cannot reach the comment. The member always lands at the top of the feed. Bonus copy bug: `message: \`${session.user.name} liked your post\`` fires for letters too.

title: editPost caps plain posts at 5000 chars while createPost accepts 20000 — a legitimately long post becomes permanently uneditable
claim_actual: postSchema is a flat `content: z.string().min(1).max(20000)` for BOTH kinds, and the composer has no length limit on the contentEditable (only a soft "This might make a lovely Letter" nudge at 600 chars). So a member can post 5001-20000 chars as a plain post through the normal UI. editPost then enforces `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) return { error: ... }` — opening the edit dialog on such a post and saving (even with zero changes) is refused with "Content must be between 1 and 5000 characters".
evidence: validators.ts:154 `content: z.string().min(1, "Post cannot be empty").max(20000)` with no kind conditionality; actions.ts:395-399 `const isLetter = post.kind === "letter"; const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) { return { error: \`Content must be between 1 and ${cap} characters\` }; }`. create-post-form.tsx has no maxLength on the editor (LETTER_NUDGE_LEN = 600 is explicitly "no red numbers, no limits messaging: just a hint").
orchestrator_note: editPost validator maxes 5000; createPost 20000.

title: A letter draft's city audience is invisible and unchangeable at the desk: editPost drops cityScope and the desk never hydrates it
claim_actual: Three interlocking gaps. (1) editPost's update writes only `{ content, title?, images? }` — cityScope is never read from the form, so choosing a city (or 'Everyone') while resuming a draft is silently ignored. (2) The edit page's select fetches `id, kind, status, authorId, title, content, images, isHidden` — not cityScope — and LetterDesk/CreatePostForm have no initialCityScope prop; `audienceCity` always initialises to null, so a draft saved as 'Bangalore only' renders with no audience chip, looking like 'Everyone'. (3) Even in one sitting: first "Save as draft" stores cityScope via createPost, then onDraftSaved does router.replace to the edit route, remounting the desk with audienceCity reset to null — the chip the writer just set disappears. Net effect: a member can publish a letter believing it goes to everyone when it is city-limited, or believe they limited it when their change was dropped.
evidence: feed/actions.ts editPost: `await prisma.post.update({ where: { id: postId }, data: { content, ...(isLetter ? { title: title?.trim() || null } : {}), ...imagesUpdate } })` — no cityScope. create-post-form.tsx: `const [audienceCity, setAudienceCity] = useState<string | null>(null);` with no initial prop; handleSubmit only does `if (audienceCity) formData.set("cityScope", audienceCity)` which editPost ignores. letters/[id]/edit/page.tsx select list omits cityScope. publishDraft flips status only, preserving whatever cityScope sits on the row.
orchestrator_note: editPost omits cityScope from the update; edit page does not load it.

title: Contact-editor stale closure: removing a phone/link/email row saves the PRE-removal list, so the removed value silently survives
claim_actual: The UI removes the row, but the server write persists the OLD list including the removed row. On the next page load the 'removed' phone number is back on the member's public Get in touch sheet.
evidence: contacts-editor.tsx remove button (lines 226-229): `onClick={() => { onChange(rows.filter((r) => r.id !== row.id)); onCommit(); }}`. `onChange` is `setContactRows` and `onCommit` is `commitContacts` from letterhead-profile.tsx:423-429: `function commitContacts() { void run(async () => { const result = await updateContactMethods(rowsToPayload(contactRows)); ... }) }`. `commitContacts` closes over the `contactRows` state variable of the render in which the click happened — `setContactRows(next)` has not re-rendered yet when `onCommit()` executes in the same event handler, so `rowsToPayload(contactRows)` serialises the PRE-removal array and `updateContactMethods` writes it. The success then calls `router.refresh()`, but the client `contactRows` state (initialised once in `useState(() => draft ? buildRows(draft.contacts) : [])`, letterhead-profile.tsx:332-334) is preserved across refresh, so the UI keeps showing the row as gone while the DB still has it. The blur-commit path (PenValue onCommit) is safe because keystroke onChange events re-render before blur; only the same-tick onChange+onCommit of the remove button hits the stale closure. Removing a phone number is a privacy gesture: the member believes it is off their profile while every verified viewer still gets it in Get in touch and in the vCard.
orchestrator_note: commitContacts reads a stale contactRows closure captured before the removal setState.

title: A member cannot remove their profile email: clearing it saves displayEmail=null and the page then falls back to exposing the private sign-in email
claim_actual: Removing the email row (even when the stale-closure bug above doesn't intervene) writes displayEmail=null, after which the profile serves the member's LOGIN email to every Stage-2 viewer: page.tsx:177 `const contactEmail = user.displayEmail?.trim() || user.email;`. On next edit, buildRows (contacts-editor.tsx:126-127: `if (source.displayEmail || source.email) rows.push({ ... value: source.displayEmail || source.email })`) re-seeds the row from the account email, so the 'removed' row reappears. The X on the email row is a no-op that looks like a privacy control.
evidence: The remove button renders unconditionally for every row kind (contacts-editor.tsx:223-235, no `row.kind !== "email"` guard). rowsToPayload (lines 94-106) returns `displayEmail: first("email")` = null when the row is gone; updateContactMethods (profile-actions.ts:229) stores `displayEmail: parsed.data.displayEmail || null`. The profile page and vCard then use the fallback `user.displayEmail?.trim() || user.email` (page.tsx:177, 274), so the sign-in address ships to all verified members. There is no showEmail/showPhone column in schema.prisma (grep confirms zero hits), so no opt-out exists anywhere.

title: A Catch-up whose Round publishes while paused never schedules another Round; resume does not re-arm nextOpensAt and there is no manual recovery
claim_actual: If the live Round crosses answering->preparing->published while the Catch-up is paused (the clock advance in advanceEdition does not stop for paused Catch-ups), nextOpensAt is never written. resumeCatchup only flips status back to active. openNextRoundIfDue requires a non-null nextOpensAt, and nothing else in the codebase ever sets it, so the Catch-up sits 'active' forever with no future Round, no error, and no Keeper control to start one.
evidence: In applyEditionAction the publish transition guards the schedule write on live status: `if (action.setsNextOpensAt && meta.catchupStatus === "active") { await tx.catchup.update({ where: { id: meta.catchupId }, data: { nextOpensAt: addCadenceGap(now, meta.cadence) } }); }` (catchups.ts:802-806); publishNow has the identical guard `if (edition.catchup.status === "active")` (actions.ts:1054). pauseCatchup writes only `data: { status: "paused" }` (actions.ts:591) and resumeCatchup writes only `data: { status: "active" }` (actions.ts:618) — neither touches nextOpensAt. openNextRoundIfDue begins `const opensAt = catchup.nextOpensAt; if (!opensAt || now.getTime() < opensAt.getTime()) return;` (catchups.ts:908-909), and a repo-wide grep shows the ONLY writers of nextOpensAt are the two publish paths (both gated on active) and endCatchup (sets null). advanceDueCatchups also filters `where: { status: "active", nextOpensAt: { lte: now } }` (catchups.ts:971), so a null nextOpensAt is permanently invisible to the sweep. Meanwhile editions of paused Catch-ups DO keep advancing: the editions query at catchups.ts:956-964 does not filter on catchup.status, so a Round in flight at pause time will publish (members even get the catchup_published notification) — exactly the sequence that strands the series.

title: Pausing or ending a Catch-up does not stop the in-flight Round: it keeps advancing, sending daily reminders, and publishes itself
claim_actual: advanceDueCatchups selects live editions with no filter on catchup.status, and applyEditionAction only consults catchupStatus for setsNextOpensAt. So a paused/ended Catch-up's Round keeps auto-advancing collecting->answering->preparing->published, keeps firing catchup_answers_open/catchup_published to every member, and non-answerers keep receiving a DAILY catchup_reminder for the whole 7-10 day window. Meanwhile the home replaces the entire console with 'This Catch-up is paused.' (no Answer CTA, no question list), yet the page header still prints the live countdown ('{name} · 3 days left') above that banner, the notification links to /catchups/[id]/answer still work, and submitEntry accepts answers (it checks only membership + edition.status). Pause also does not stop the clock: a Keeper pausing mid-answering to 'freeze' silently loses the window, and resume does not shift deadlines.
evidence: catchups.ts:956-963 'const editions = await prisma.catchupEdition.findMany({ where: { status: { in: ["collecting", "answering", "preparing"] }, catchup: scope } ...' where scope filters only membership; catchups.ts:802 'if (action.setsNextOpensAt && meta.catchupStatus === "active")' is the ONLY status check in applyEditionAction, and the reminder branch at 826-833 fires notify.notifyReminder unconditionally; catchup-home-shell.tsx:57-63 'catchupStatus !== "active" ? <PausedOrEndedBanner .../>' replaces the whole left console; [catchupId]/page.tsx:512-516 header title uses result.edition?.countdownLabel with no catchupStatus guard; actions.ts submitEntry 1115-1121 checks membership and edition.status !== "answering" but never edition.catchup.status; answer/page.tsx has no catchup.status check either. The banner's own copy 'No new Round opens until it is resumed' admits pause only gates openNextRoundIfDue.

title: A Catch-up nobody adds questions to still runs the full cycle: answering opens with zero questions and everyone is reminded to answer nothing
claim_actual: computeStatus/planNextAction advance collecting->answering purely on questionsCloseAt with no prompt-count guard, firing catchup_answers_open to all members. With zero prompts nobody CAN answer, so every member is a non-answerer and receives a daily catchup_reminder for the 7-day window; at close, the too-few rule extends once (+3 more days of dailies, another answers-open blast), then it publishes an empty Round ('This Round did not gather any questions.') and notifies 'ready to read'. openNextRoundIfDue only requires latest.status === 'published', so a fresh empty Round opens next cadence and the whole loop repeats forever until a human ends the catch-up. The /answer page's zero-prompt state even says 'Check back once the Keeper has added a few questions' during answering, when adding questions is impossible (submitPrompt requires status collecting). Note the UI knows better: OpenAnsweringButton only renders when a prompt exists (shell line 121-125), but the clock path has no such guard.
evidence: catchups.ts:505-514 'if (next === "answering") { return { kind: "transition", ..., patch: answeringPatch(ed, now), notify: "catchup_answers_open" ... } }' with no prompt count in scope (planNextAction's inputs are timing + entryCount only); catchups.ts:908-913 'if (!latest || latest.status !== "published") return;' is openNextRoundIfDue's only content gate; catchups-notify.ts:139-141 non-answerers = all members when entries are zero; answer/page.tsx:199-207 zero-prompt card copy 'Check back once the Keeper has added a few questions to answer.' while edition.status === 'answering'; actions.ts:692-694 submitPrompt refuses when status !== 'collecting'.

title: Enrolment is unilateral and irreversible: a Keeper can add anyone, who then gets cycle notifications forever with no way to leave
claim_actual: The only membership-removal path is removeCatchupMember, which is Keeper-only (loadKeeperScope) and explicitly refuses self-removal ('You cannot remove yourself.'); no leave/exit action exists anywhere in the feature (the only groupMember.deleteMany in the app is that Keeper action). The reminder pref 'off' silences only the daily catchup_reminder, and even that is bypassed by Keeper nudges (bypassOff); catchup_questions_open, catchup_answers_open and catchup_published go to ALL group members unconditionally, every cycle, on a recurring cadence, forever. So a member who wants out of a monthly catch-up they were added to must personally ask a Keeper, and until then keeps being notified monthly for life.
evidence: actions.ts:1355 'if (userId === session.user.id) return { error: "You cannot remove yourself." };' inside the Keeper-gated removeCatchupMember; grep confirms no other groupMember delete in src/ outside demo seed; catchups-notify.ts:82-93 notifyQuestionsOpen and 177-188 notifyPublished derive recipients from groupMemberIds with no pref filter; 142 'if (!ctx.bypassOff)' shows the off pref is skipped for Keeper nudges; actions.ts:420-434 createCatchupWithPeople enrols invitedIds directly as GroupMember rows with no acceptance step.

title: deletion-scheduled emails can never be sent: drain eligibleKinds omits the kind, so every account-deletion confirmation / takeover alarm sits queued forever
claim_actual: The drain can never select the row. `eligibleKinds` is `["verify", "reset", "password-changed"]` or `["reset", "password-changed"]` — 'deletion-scheduled' appears in neither branch, and findFirst filters `kind: { in: eligibleKinds }`. The only other caller of claimAndSend is verificationMailState, which reads `kind: "verify"` rows only. So every deletion-scheduled row sits status 'queued' forever: the member who requested deletion never gets the written confirmation, a victim of an account takeover never gets the alarm during the 60-day undo window, the admin panel's 'Waiting to go' count is permanently inflated, admin retryMail cannot help (requeued rows are still ineligible) and dismissMail refuses non-'failed' rows. After 180 days the retention sweep silently deletes the never-sent row (deleteMany on createdAt with no status filter).
evidence: email-queue.ts:468-469: `const eligibleKinds = live.verifyRemaining > 0 ? ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] : ["reset", "password-changed"];` and 472: `where: { status: "queued", kind: { in: eligibleKinds }, ... }`. Yet the kind is fully wired everywhere else: type MailKind includes it (53), `"deletion-scheduled": 20` in PRIORITY (68), an ENQUEUE_LIMIT entry (281), a render branch (394), and settings/actions.ts:338-341 enqueues it: `await enqueueMail({ kind: "deletion-scheduled", to: me.email, userId, ... })`. verificationMailState's findFirst is `where: { userId, kind: "verify" }` (565-566), so it can never send it either.
orchestrator_note: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED: MailKind includes 'deletion-scheduled' but eligibleKinds is always ['verify','reset','password-changed'].

title: A bounce/complaint webhook flips a 'sent' row to 'failed', which resurrects daily-budget slots and lets the app send past Resend's real 100/day cap
claim_actual: dailyBudget counts `{ status: "sent", sentAt: { gte: startOfUtcDay() } }`. The webhook's bounce patch sets `status: "failed"` (and complaint likewise) while leaving sentAt in place — so every same-day bounce or complaint removes a message from 'used' that Resend already counted against the real quota. Each bounce resurrects one phantom budget slot. The webhook file's own motivation is launch mail 'bouncing off stale addresses' in the hundreds; a dozen same-day bounces already exceeds the entire 5-message headroom, after which the drain keeps sending while Resend hard-rejects — and each rejection burns attempts toward terminal 'failed' (see the Critical retry finding), failing exactly the messages the reserve exists to protect. mailHealth.sentToday undercounts the same way, so the admin panel under-reports the day.
evidence: route.ts:117-118: bounce patch includes `status: "failed"` (and 128 for complaints), with no compensating field; email-queue.ts:258-260: `const used = await prisma.outboundEmail.count({ where: { status: "sent", sentAt: { gte: startOfUtcDay() } } });`. The margin's whole justification (comment 74-79) is absorbing miscounts of ~a retry or two, not a launch-day bounce rate.
orchestrator_note: dailyBudget counts by status; webhook status='failed' on a delivered row frees a slot.

title: Drain concurrency is unbounded: every authenticated page view and every enqueue kicks a full drain, so launch traffic fans past Resend's rate
claim_actual: There is no global coordination at all. Every authenticated page view runs `after(drainMailQueue)` (layout.tsx:63-69) and every enqueueMail calls scheduleDrain (350). K overlapping passes do not collapse: when two race for the head row, the loser gets 'lost-claim' and simply moves to the NEXT row (comment at 481-482), so K concurrent passes send K different rows in parallel. At launch (steady page views over a 100+ row backlog) that is a self-inflicted 429 storm against a 2 rps provider limit — and every 429 burns an attempt toward terminal failure (Critical finding above). Independently, the budget check is per-pass check-then-send: rows in status 'sending' are not counted by dailyBudget (it counts 'sent' only), so with K passes in flight the cap can be exceeded by up to K messages, past the 5-message headroom, producing hard provider rejections.
evidence: layout.tsx:63-65: `after(async () => { try { await drainMailQueue(); } ...` on every render of the authenticated layout; email-queue.ts:452/462: `const budget = await dailyBudget(); ... const live = await dailyBudget(); if (live.remaining === 0) break;` — both reads count `status: "sent"` rows only (258-260), never in-flight 'sending' rows; 481-482: `// lost-claim: another process took the row ... the loop just looks for the next one.` — the mechanism by which concurrent passes parallelize instead of deduplicating.

title: Payment success callback has no error handling: a thrown confirmContribution after money moved leaves the button stuck on 'Opening' forever, no receipt
claim_actual: Neither `await startContribution(amount)` (line 119) nor `await confirmContribution(res)` inside the Razorpay `handler` (line 161) has a try/catch. A server action that THROWS (as opposed to returning `{error}`) rejects the client-side promise; `pay()` and the async `handler` are fire-and-forget callbacks, so the rejection is unhandled, `setWorking(false)` never runs, no toast appears, and the button shows the 'Opening' spinner permanently. On the confirm path the member has just paid: the modal closes, then nothing — no toast, no redirect to /pick-bird, a dead button. Server side makes the throw realistic: in startContribution the `prisma.user.findUnique` phone read at actions.ts:81-84 sits OUTSIDE the try block that starts at line 86, so a transient DB error there throws to the client instead of returning the friendly `{error}` the rest of the action is built around. `auth()` throwing, a Vercel invocation error, or plain network loss in the seconds after payment (common during India UPI app-switch flows) all take the same unhandled path.
evidence: support-contribute.tsx:119 `const started = await startContribution(amount as number);` — bare await, the enclosing `pay()` has try/catch only around `loadCheckout()`. Handler, lines 161-167: `handler: async (res: RazorpaySuccess) => { const confirmed = await confirmContribution(res); if ("error" in confirmed) { setWorking(false); ... }` — the error-object branch is handled, the rejection branch is not, and the success path deliberately never resets `working` (comment line 173-174: "`working` stays true through the navigation"), so a rejection strands it true. actions.ts:81-86: `const profile = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: session.user.id }, select: { phone: true } });` followed by `try {` — the read is outside the try whose catch returns `{ error: "We could not reach the payment gateway..." }`.

title: When the webhook (not the browser) records a payment, the supporter gets nothing: no notification, no email, no path to the promised bird perk
claim_actual: The webhook's payment.captured branch updates the Contribution row and does nothing else — no Notification row, no email, no revalidation. Meanwhile /support deliberately never links /pick-bird (page.tsx:121-126: 'the ONLY way in is the redirect after a successful payment'). So the exact scenario the webhook was built for — Android kills the tab during the UPI app switch, or the payer closes the 3-D Secure page — ends with money recorded, the recovery bar advanced, and the supporter locked out of the perk they were promised ('Anyone who contributes picks their own bird') unless they guess the /pick-bird URL. The owner's no-standing-link decision covered members who completed the flow; it did not consider the flow dying between payment and redirect. Compounding cases that hit the same dead end with the tab still open: confirmContribution returning 'Not authenticated' (session expired mid-payment) or the finding-1 throw — the row still goes paid via webhook, the redirect still never happens.
evidence: webhook/route.ts:72-83: the captured branch is exactly one `prisma.contribution.update({ ... status: "paid" ... })` — grep confirms no Notification/OutboundEmail write anywhere in the route. support/page.tsx:121-125: 'No standing door to /pick-bird here, even for members who have already contributed: the ONLY way in is the redirect after a successful payment (owner).' The redirect lives only in the browser handler, support-contribute.tsx:177 `router.push("/pick-bird")`. /pick-bird/page.tsx:52-67 would ADMIT this member (paid sum ≥ threshold, fresh unspent pick) — the gate works; the door is what is missing.

title: Missing indexes on hot count FKs: Like.postId, Comment.parentId, PollVote.postId/pollOptionId, CommentLike.commentId, PhotoLove.photoId, Post.authorId
claim_actual: Like's only index is `@@unique([userId, postId])` (schema.prisma:465), which leads with userId and cannot serve postId-only predicates. Every feed page (`_count: { select: { comments: {...}, likes: true } }`, feed/actions.ts:859), the letters index (letters/page.tsx:58), saved posts (feed/actions.ts:996), and the 'liked' sort (`orderBy: { likes: { _count: "desc" } }`, feed/actions.ts:893) all count likes per post. Prisma executes relation counts as a grouped aggregate/lateral count on Like WHERE postId — with no usable index that is a full scan of the Like table per request. Plausible 2,000-user row count: ~20k posts x ~10 likes = ~200k Like rows, rescanned on every feed/letters/saved page load; the offset-paged 'liked' sort additionally re-aggregates the whole table per page. Worse: `prisma.$transaction([report.deleteMany, user.delete])` in account-purge.ts:99 cascades User→Post→Like; Postgres runs the FK cascade per deleted Post row, each doing an unindexed lookup WHERE postId = <id> — an author with 500 posts triggers ~500 sequential full scans of a 200k-row table inside one transaction, which can run for minutes, hold a pgbouncer pooled connection, and fail the retention sweep's purge.
evidence: schema.prisma Like model in full: `model Like { id String @id @default(cuid()); userId String; postId String; user User @relation(...); post Post @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade); @@unique([userId, postId]) }` — no other index. Feed include at feed/actions.ts:859: `_count: { select: { comments: { where: { isHidden: false, deletedAt: null } }, likes: true } }` runs on every loadPosts call (PAGE_SIZE 20, line 762). Sort at :891-894: `sortBy === "liked" ? { likes: { _count: "desc" } } : ...` with `skip: offset` (:900). A btree on (userId, postId) can only satisfy WHERE postId=? via a full index scan; the comments count by contrast has `@@index([postId, isHidden])` (schema:454), showing the pattern was applied to Comment but missed on Like.
orchestrator_note: Uniques lead with userId so per-target counts seq-scan; Comment.parentId thread reads full-scan; Post.authorId profile reads full-scan. See CL-13 dossier.

title: Place gazetteer search full-scans all 234,934 rows on every keystroke of 4+ chars: the altNames ILIKE arm in an OR defeats the expression index
claim_actual: For queries of 4+ characters (i.e. most of every city name typed: "chen", "chenn", "chennai") the WHERE clause becomes `indexable-arm OR indexable-arm OR altNames ILIKE '%q%'`. Postgres can only use a BitmapOr when EVERY arm of an OR is indexable; `"altNames"` has no index of any kind (schema.prisma:636 is a bare `String?`, no migration creates one — verified across all of prisma/migrations-manual/), so the planner falls back to a sequential scan of the full 234,934-row Place table, evaluating `lower()` twice plus an ILIKE over a long comma-joined text column per row, per keystroke, per member.
evidence: src/app/api/places/search/route.ts:99-109: `const altNamesClause = raw.length >= 4 ? Prisma.sql`OR "altNames" ILIKE ${containsPattern} ESCAPE '\\'` : Prisma.empty;` folded into `WHERE lower("asciiName") LIKE lower(${prefixPattern}) ESCAPE '\\' OR lower("name") LIKE lower(${prefixPattern}) ESCAPE '\\' ${altNamesClause}`. The only indexes on Place are `CREATE INDEX ... ON "Place" (lower("asciiName") text_pattern_ops)` and the same for name (2026-07-18-round6.sql:30-31) — grep for `pg_trgm|GIN|altNames` across prisma/migrations-manual/*.sql finds no altNames index. The route's own comment admits the arm "degrades to a sequential scan" but treats the 4-char gate as the mitigation; 4+ chars is the COMMON case for a real city name, not the rare one. The arithmetic: Supabase Free plan (docs/OPERATIONS.md:57 "Supabase's free plan has no automatic backups") means Nano compute with Supavisor's default transaction-mode pool_size of ~15 server connections. A 234k-row seq scan with per-row lower()+ILIKE on shared nano CPU is realistically 80-200ms. Ceiling = 15 slots / 0.15s ≈ 100 scans/s. A member typing fires ~3 requests/s (the rate limit at line 84 deliberately allows 120/min); so ~15-25 members simultaneously typing in the LocationPicker — exactly the launch-day onboarding shape, and src/lib/email-queue.ts:18-20 records the owner "expects more than 100 signups on the first day" — occupies every server connection, and EVERY other query in the app (feed, login, notification counts) queues behind the scans at the pooler. Combined with the missing timeouts (next finding) the queue manifests as site-wide hangs, not errors.

title: Directory page serializes every located member into map props on every load and every filter change (~1-2MB) with no take/pagination

title: Visit and SearchLog (identifiable presence telemetry) have no retention: absent from the sweep, prune.mjs, and the retention table — unbounded growth
claim_actual: runRetentionSweep deletes from exactly seven tables (adminMessages, reports, contributions, notifications, loginAttempts, auditLogs, outboundEmails — retention.ts:73-107) plus due accounts; prune.mjs touches only Notification. title: Supabase Free plan cannot carry 2,000 members: egress alone lands multiples over the 5GB/month cap (per-request session findUnique + full-member directory)
claim_actual: The project is on the Supabase Free plan (docs/OPERATIONS.md:57 states it outright), whose bundled egress is 5GB/month across database + storage. title: Every server-rendered date shows the UTC calendar day, not IST: anything timestamped 00:00-05:30 IST renders one day early, sitewide
claim_actual: formatDisplayDate is `new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })` with no timeZone option, and formatTimeAgo's >4-week fallback is `date.toLocaleDateString("en-IN", {...})` with no timeZone. Both are called from genuine React Server Components running in UTC on Vercel: letters/page.tsx line 163 `metaLine(batchLine(l.author), formatDisplayDate(l.createdAt))` and letters/[id]/page.tsx line 188 `date={formatDisplayDate(letter.createdAt)}` (neither file is "use client"). A letter created at 00:30 IST 15 June is 19:00 UTC 14 June, so the server renders "14 Jun 2026" for every viewer, permanently. 00:00–05:30 IST is ~23% of the clock and includes India's late-night posting hours. The same helpers are also used server-side across admin pages (admin/page.tsx, admin/audit, admin/support, admin/catchups) and messages/thread-list.tsx (no "use client" directive; whether it inherits a client boundary needs one check).

title: Admin analytics Rhythms heatmap applies AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata' in the wrong direction, shifting every hour bucket by ~11 hours
claim_actual: The query applies `"endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'` directly to a timestamp-without-time-zone. In Postgres that means "interpret this wall time AS Kolkata local", producing an instant 5h30 EARLIER in UTC; EXTRACT then reads it in the session timezone (UTC on Supabase). A 19:30-IST visit (stored 14:00 UTC wall) buckets at hour 8 instead of 19 — 11 hours off, with DOW shifting wrongly near midnight too. The peak hour the page tells the owner to schedule Catch-up email against is fiction.
evidence: admin-analytics.ts:584-585: `SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM "endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::int AS dow, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::int AS hour`. schema.prisma Visit model: `endedAt DateTime @default(now())` with no @db.Timestamptz, i.e. `timestamp(3) without time zone` holding UTC wall time (bugs.md #6 documents exactly this column class). Postgres semantics: `timestamp AT TIME ZONE zone` -> timestamptz (interprets AS that zone); the correct incantation for a UTC wall time is `("endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'`. The component then prints "Busiest: {day} around {hour} IST. Worth matching the Catch-up email to it." (heatmap.tsx:75-87) — an explicit recommendation drawn from wrong buckets. This is the 6h IST class the audit brief predicts, in the one query that tried to handle it.
orchestrator_note: Double-conversion / wrong direction on a timestamp-without-tz column.

title: The notification bell badge is frozen for the whole browsing session: (main) layout computes unreadCount only on hard loads; badge only ever falls
claim_actual: Three compounding facts make the badge correct only at the moment of a full page load. title: joinBatchGroup is check-then-create with no unique on Group.name: concurrent same-batch signups (launch day) create duplicate 'Batch of Y' groups, splitting the batch
claim_actual: The rule is backed by nothing: Group has no unique on name (schema.prisma:191-208 — the code admits it: "Group.name is not unique in the schema, so match by exact name"). auth/actions.ts:215-230 is a findFirst → create with no P2002 possible: two members of the same batch registering concurrently (launch day is explicitly expected to exceed 100 signups) both miss the findFirst and both create a group named "Batch of 2010". From then on every later signup's `findFirst({ where: { name } })` — with no orderBy, so arbitrary but sticky — lands members in one or the other: the batch is permanently split into two groups whose members cannot see each other's group posts (loadPosts requires GroupMember membership for group feeds, feed/actions.ts:784-790). Nothing ever detects or repairs the split.
evidence: auth/actions.ts:215-230: `let group = await prisma.group.findFirst({ where: { name }, select: { id: true } }); if (!group) { group = await prisma.group.create({ data: { name, ..., creatorId: userId }, ...}); }` — classic TOCTOU. schema.prisma Group model (lines 191-208) carries only `@@index([visibility, createdAt])`, no @@unique on name. Contrast with the same file's registerUser, which the same commit hardened with a P2002 catch for the user-email race (auth/actions.ts:164-169) — the group half of the same signup flow was left unguarded.

title: 'Most loved' collection sort has no deterministic tiebreaker: offset pagination duplicates and drops photos, and produces duplicate React keys
claim_actual: Rows tied on love count (which is almost all of them: most photos have 0-2 loves) are returned in arbitrary, non-stable order per query. Page 2 (skip 24) re-runs the sort and can return rows already shown on page 1 and omit others. The client appends with setPhotos(prev => [...prev, ...data.photos]) keyed by key={p.id}, so duplicates also collide as React keys.
evidence: actions.ts:466-471: `const orderBy = opts?.sortBy === "oldest" ? { createdAt: "asc" as const } : opts?.sortBy === "loved" ? { loves: { _count: "desc" as const } } : { createdAt: "desc" as const };` then 473-480: `prisma.photo.findMany({ where, include: includeFor(...), orderBy, take: PAGE_SIZE + 1, skip: page * PAGE_SIZE })`. For "loved" the ONLY sort key is the aggregate count; Postgres gives no stable order for ties, and each page is a fresh query, so tied rows shuffle between pages. collection-client.tsx:399-402 renders `photos.map((p, i) => (<Tile key={p.id} ...>))` after handleLoadMore's `setPhotos((prev) => [...prev, ...data.photos])` (line 167), so a repeated id is a duplicate key. Reachable the moment the collection holds more than PAGE_SIZE=24 approved photos and someone opens the "Most loved" sort and loads more. ("newest"/"oldest" sort on createdAt is also un-tiebroken but ms-precision ties are rare; the loved sort is tied by construction.)
